messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — ran a long-context (50k token) perf pass and saw KV cache memory climb steadily; attaching a tiny profile snippet.

maria: profile snippet:
```
alloc histogram: 64B x 120k, 256B x 34k, 1KB x 2.9k
slab fragmentation ~ 22%
live_kv_slots: 1.2M
```

jonah: Oof. Is this after the allocator change (chunk_coalesce=on)?

maria: yes. Coalesce lowered peak allocations but left lots of small holes. Eviction rate is low but reuse is poor — we keep allocating new 64B blocks instead of reusing nearby 128B holes.

lee: Could be block-size granularity. Current allocator biases power-of-two sizes; repeated small refills create many tiny allocations. What about a small "stash" for sub-128B fragments that prefers reuse over full compaction?

anya: What's the workload distribution here — mostly long single sequences or many short chats interleaved?

maria: Mostly long sequences (>20k) with repeated attention patterns. During tail generation we end up with small batch sizes which prevents effective natural compaction.

jonah: Two approaches: adaptive block sizing (grow small blocks into 128B on reused allocations) or a background compactor targeting high-frag buckets. Background compaction historically adds CPU; want to avoid hurting latency.

lee: We experimented briefly with background compaction — it competes for CPU but the wall-time hit was acceptable in off-peak. Idea: holdback heuristic — only compact when hole density > 30% for a bucket set and maintain a tiny LRU stash for recent small frees.

maria: I ran a microbench on staging traces: stash-only reduces new allocs by ~18% and latency was flat; background compaction reduced steady memory by ~12% but added ~4% CPU overhead. Numbers: baseline mem 5.4GB -> stash 4.45GB -> compaction 4.75GB.

anya: Nice. Combine them: stash as first defense, compaction as fallback once stash pressure/age thresholds cross. Add metrics: stash_hit_rate, stash_evictions, frag_ratio so we can observe behavior.

jonah: Also tie to kernel selection / routing: when cache fragmentation leads to eviction thrash, prefer kernel paths that minimize KV retention (shorter KV TTL) or route to a cheaper model variant to avoid a cascading memory problem.

lee: Proposed plan: 1) implement stash prototype in allocator (small per-bucket free list), 2) emit metrics (stash_hits, stash_misses, frag_ratio, compaction_run_count), 3) run A/B on staging for 48h with long-context traces. I'll open a PR for the allocator patch.

maria: Assigned to lee. Please tag infra-bot to schedule the canary suite. I'll prepare the eval traces and a short perf harness.

infra-bot: Canary run scheduled: kv-stash-proto - run_id 2026-03-19-001 :white_check_mark:

anya: Also add a perf scenario that simulates small-batch tail gen where stash matters most; want to be sure stash doesn't introduce tail-latency regressions on cold starts.

jonah: Agreed. If stash looks healthy we can defer heavy compaction. If not, we'll prototype an incremental compactor that sweeps only high-density buckets and stops when mem wins are marginal.

lee: Understood. PR will include microbench scripts and a simple flamegraph. I'll post perf numbers in this thread when the canary completes.

maria: :thumbsup:
